BLIP_field_controls.scope: Additional predeclared offline sensitivity: likelihood/scalar interventions on a frozen CPU head, no model fitting; nonlinear contributions are not additive causal fractions

distribution_shift.expert_exposure_causal_attribution: UNRESOLVED: no expert-training counterfactual or independent unseen-expert dataset

fitting: five RGB-group-disjoint TRAIN folds; OOF epoch selection; final full TRAIN refit except declared learning curves; two TRAIN/TEST RGB copies excluded
interpretation_limits: Learning curves hold epochs rather than optimizer steps constant.
Random-label negative-control OOF fits use seeded random permutations; its final refit uses a cyclic permutation. Interpret random-label evidence primarily on OOF.
Synthetic omission probes are a privileged partial-dataset subset.
Crop remedies also change scale/distortion; lost pixels alone do not prove a particular F1 loss.
Supplementary constant-update comparisons partially control the constant-epoch learning-curve limitation; one seed, intervals include zero.
Reported historical combined router is distinct from the token-head baseline used for matched interventions.
Ground-truth count substitution is privileged, nondeployable and not an additive attribution of causes.

metric.ignore: source native256 care/ignore; ignored predictions excluded; all images retained
metric.matching: casefold lexical multiset; duplicates/punctuation retained; no IoU
metric.name: exact_casefold_word_multiset_micro_F1

H1.intervention: Smaller capacity and stronger decay have no supported positive held-out F1 effect in tested grid.
H1.unresolved: Generalization remains limited; overfitting is not established as the dominant remediable cause.

H2.intervention: Padded/stretched refits have no supported final router F1 gain. Foil preference is not OCR accuracy.
H2.observed: Native center cropping removes boundary markers. Complete-word stretch improves held-out correctness AUC.
H2.unresolved: Improved word evidence alone is insufficient for demonstrated relative-expert ranking gains.

H3.intervention: Scalar-only and likelihood-only controls isolate a misleading scalar response and weak omission sensitivity.
H3.observed: Known extra FN often fails to reduce predicted light-expert utility; BLIP head can react in the opposite direction.
H3.unresolved: Synthetic privileged omissions are outside the natural error distribution; foundation-model inability is not proved.

H4.intervention: Strictly positive affine score transforms cannot alter fixed-quota selections.
H4.observed: Eligible positive-utility rate differs by 12.20pp between TRAIN and TEST and persists after count/confidence matching.
H4.unresolved: Expert-training exposure is not causally isolated; independent expert-unseen evaluation is needed.

H5.intervention: Lowering bypass reduces measured loss but forfeits compute savings; predicted-positive gates still do not beat all-DeepSolo.
H5.observed: TRAIN OOF chooses zero bypass for all five original arms in the tested quota grid. TEST GT oracle can improve at 50%; TRAIN GT oracle cannot.
H5.unresolved: Fifty-percent bypass is feasible under TEST oracle; deployed ranking remains the limitation.

H6.intervention: Removing auxiliary loss or aligning it to lexical primary labels has no supported positive F1 effect.
H6.observed: 79/6021 TRAIN and 19/1496 TEST primary TPs have negative spatial auxiliary labels under declared assignment.
H6.unresolved: Mismatch exists but has not been shown to explain the main performance gap.
